samples.marker_line: SEO doorway: cloaked redirects; tighten navigation and decoy rules
samples.verdict_evidence: The concealed search-only redirect, non-search 404 route and encoded browsing-data export are inconsistent with an ordinary drug-information page. No provenance establishing an authorized analytics/SEO experiment was provided.
execution_trace: The outer Hiwagotu decoder converts hash-delimited decimal codes into a complete script element and passes it to document.write.

The decoded script selects search-engine referrers by engine name and search-query parameter. Google/Yahoo simulations navigate to medipharmtour.com; direct/unrelated visitors navigate to same-host /404.html.

key() combines the full referrer, current document URL and separators. encode() hex-encodes the result and appends it as the r query value to the remote navigation. The search term parsed into q is unused; the remote query is fixed to bacitracin.

The visible WordPress-like pharmaceutical keyword page and unrelated hyperlink catalogue act as SEO bait; its external stylesheet/feed/favicon references are ordinary page resources and were preserved.
samples.coverage_and_limits: Two hostile results now distinguish packed search-referrer traffic diversion from a 404-decoy path. Numeric concealment stays suspicious. The covert referrer/current-page export is verified manually but not independently matched as hostile: cleave facts exposes no decoded hash-decimal script or HTML flow graph. Raw hidden URL/source/assignment combinations were investigated and added only as supported notable observations; they cannot prove data flow. A third hostile finding would require a general hash-decimal decoder/flow projection rather than another redirect co-occurrence.

samples.marker_line: CI publish bridge: steals registry tokens; detect downloaded launch
samples.verdict_evidence: The direct registry-secret HTTP body upload and planted Bash startup hook are decisive. A CI publish helper has no ordinary reason to export raw publishing credentials to that receiver; invocation of its downloaded executable is statically linked. No authorized exercise context was provided.
execution_trace: Writes a quoted-heredoc shell hook into RUNNER_TEMP (or /tmp), then appends BASH_ENV=<hook> to GITHUB_ENV. Later Bash steps source the hook when the runner exports the new environment.

When either publishing-token variable is nonempty, printenv selects PYPI_API_TOKEN and NPM_TOKEN and pipes their values into curl --data-binary @- to an external receiver. The body is the credentials, not an Authorization header or intended registry publish request.
Creates the helper parent directory, downloads a file into IMPLANT, chmods the same variable target +x, then invokes that exact path with checkout metadata and initial-ci-emit/config64 arguments.

The config decodes to a runtime schema, campaign/profile, hidden HOME-relative state path, and a separate control URL. These are configuration references; they do not establish implant persistence, payload behavior, or propagation.
exit 1 aborts the real publish step. The comment about republishing under another identity cannot establish that unavailable payload action.
samples.coverage_and_limits: Three hostile findings cover registry-token upload, CI startup authority abuse, and downloaded-file activation during token theft. Same-variable tree-sitter binding supplies download-to-launch evidence, including the environment-prefixed command. Final payload was unavailable; no additional hostile behavior is inferred from config names/comments.

samples.identification: Concealed VS Code folder-open remote HTA task
samples.marker_line: VS Code task: concealed remote HTA autorun; fix task-scope matching
samples.verdict_evidence: The hidden folder-open MSHTA execution under an interview-preparation label tips the likely-malicious judgment. The reserved endpoint makes this a nonworking template on public DNS; source/deployment evidence of an authorized exercise is missing.
execution_trace: The single shell task commands mshta.exe with an HTTPS HTA URL, requests background execution, hides the task from selection, suppresses terminal reveal/echo/focus, and activates on folderOpen.

This is a configured Windows script-host execution chain disguised as interview workspace preparation. No ordinary build/prepare command or local workspace operation explains the remote HTA invocation.

The .invalid destination prevents a normal public fetch. VS Code workspace trust and automatic-task permission are not supplied; no runtime success or trust bypass is claimed. The structure remains an attack recipe without evidence establishing a harmless fixture origin.
samples.coverage_and_limits: One distinct hostile operation is present: a remote MSHTA command on folder open. Concealment remains suspicious, and generic MSHTA fetch/interpret behavior is notable. Attempted a structural JSON query, but the engine has no JSON tree-sitter grammar; two serialized task-object orderings bind command and trigger without joining different tasks. No additional payload bytes exist, and the .invalid endpoint provides no further stage; inventing two more hostile traits would duplicate activation or infer unknown behavior.

analysis_method: Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md before analysis.

Decoded and traced the complete HTML script in isolated QuickJS without host I/O; exercised direct, unrelated, Google and Yahoo referrers.

Decoded the bridge config; traced startup-file creation, GITHUB_ENV mutation, curl output, chmod, same-variable invocation and exit 1. Exercised the extracted token hook with sentinel variables and mocked curl/GNU printenv.
Inspected each JSON task field and command, including the .invalid endpoint and required VS Code trust/automatic-task permission.
Attempted final-stage recovery with forager; the endpoint resolves to loopback and refused connection. No final payload behavior or worm propagation is asserted.
